english: Let $H$ be the hyperbola $\dfrac{x^{2}}{3}-y^{2}=1$. A point $(x,y)$ is said to lie inside $H$ if $\dfrac{x^{2}}{3}-y^{2}>1$. For a real number $c$, let $A=(0,c)$ and $B=(2,c+2)$. The set of all values of $c$ for which the line segment $AB$ contains at least one point lying inside $H$ is the open interval $(\alpha,\beta)$. Then the value of $\alpha+\beta$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $H$ अतिपरवलय $\dfrac{x^{2}}{3}-y^{2}=1$ है। एक बिन्दु $(x,y)$ को $H$ के अन्दर स्थित कहा जाता है यदि $\dfrac{x^{2}}{3}-y^{2}>1$ हो। वास्तविक संख्या $c$ के लिए माना कि $A=(0,c)$ तथा $B=(2,c+2)$ हैं। $c$ के उन सभी मानों का समुच्चय, जिनके लिए रेखाखण्ड $AB$ पर कम से कम एक बिन्दु $H$ के अन्दर स्थित है, विवृत अन्तराल $(\alpha,\beta)$ है। तब $\alpha+\beta$ का मान ______ है।
solution: $f(x)=-\dfrac23x^{2}-2cx-c^{2}-1$, a downward parabola with vertex at $x=-\dfrac{3c}{2}$, $f\left(-\dfrac{3c}{2}\right)=\dfrac{c^{2}}{2}-1$
$c<-\dfrac43$: vertex to the right of $2$, maximum $f(2)=-\left(c^{2}+4c+\dfrac{11}{3}\right)>0\Leftrightarrow c^{2}+4c+\dfrac{11}{3}<0$
solution_full: The segment $AB$ lies on $y=x+c$ and consists of the points $(x,\,x+c)$ with $0\le x\le2$.
Such a point is inside $H$ exactly when $f(x)=\dfrac{x^{2}}{3}-(x+c)^{2}-1>0$. Expanding, $f(x)=-\dfrac23x^{2}-2cx-(c^{2}+1)$.
So the segment contains a point inside $H$ if and only if the maximum of the quadratic $f$ on $[0,2]$ is positive.
$f$ opens downward; its vertex is at $x_{0}=-\dfrac{3c}{2}$ and $f(x_{0})=-\dfrac23\cdot\dfrac{9c^{2}}{4}+3c^{2}-c^{2}-1=\dfrac{c^{2}}{2}-1$.
Case $c\ge0$: $x_{0}\le0$, so $f$ is decreasing on $[0,2]$ and the maximum is $f(0)=-c^{2}-1<0$. No point inside.
Case $-\dfrac43\le c<0$: $x_{0}\in(0,2]$, so the maximum is $\dfrac{c^{2}}{2}-1$, which is negative because $c^{2}\le\dfrac{16}{9}<2$. No point inside.
Case $c<-\dfrac43$: $x_{0}>2$, so $f$ is increasing on $[0,2]$ and the maximum is $f(2)=-\dfrac83-4c-c^{2}-1=-\left(c^{2}+4c+\dfrac{11}{3}\right)$.

$f(2)>0\Leftrightarrow c^{2}+4c+\dfrac{11}{3}<0\Leftrightarrow -2-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt3}<c<-2+\dfrac{1}{\sqrt3}$. Since $-2+\dfrac1{\sqrt3}\approx-1.42<-\dfrac43$, this whole interval lies in the present case.
Hence the required set is $\left(-2-\dfrac1{\sqrt3},\,-2+\dfrac1{\sqrt3}\right)$, so $\alpha+\beta=-4$.
Remark: the whole line $y=x+c$ enters the inside of $H$ for every $|c|>\sqrt2$, but the restriction $0\le x\le2$ removes all $c>\sqrt2$ and part of $c<-\sqrt2$.
originality_note: New: the position test S1 > 0 is applied to a segment, so the question becomes the range of a quadratic over a restricted interval with the vertex moving in and out of the interval as c varies (way 5). Closest known: condition for a line to meet a hyperbola; position of a single point with respect to a hyperbola. Different because: the segment restriction makes the answer differ from the whole-line answer |c| > sqrt2, and the case split on the vertex decides it.

concept_use.Position of a point wrt a Hyperbola: Position of a point with respect to H: a point of the segment is inside H exactly when x^2/3 - y^2 - 1 > 0, which turns the question into f(x) > 0.
concept_use.Range of a quadratic over a restricted i: The maximum of the downward quadratic f on the restricted interval [0,2] is found by locating the vertex x = -3c/2 relative to [0,2], giving the interval of c.
